summary: Eight Go modules for one deploy unit, with visible dependency drift — collapse or gate on it
description:
### Finding (architecture review R9, 2026-07-25)

The repo has eight `go.mod` files (five services, gateway, shared, smoke) under one `go.work`, one repo, one deploy unit. Nothing here is independently versioned or independently consumed. The cost is already visible as drift:

| Dependency | Pinned by |
|---|---|
| `go.opentelemetry.io/otel` | access, shared — **not** catalog, inventory, commerce, payments |
| `github.com/getkin/kin-openapi` | catalog, shared, smoke — the other three take shared's copy transitively |

So three services run whatever otel and kin-openapi versions `shared` happens to resolve, and a bump in one module silently changes behaviour in three others. Nothing in the gate notices.

### Two acceptable end states

1. **One `go.mod`.** Simplest to live with; touches every Dockerfile, `go.work` and CI job.
2. **Keep eight, add a drift check to `make check`** that fails when two modules pin different versions of a shared dependency. Smaller diff, ongoing maintenance.

The plan picks after measuring the Dockerfile/CI blast radius. Either satisfies the COS.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The shared dependency set (otel, kin-openapi, pgx, nats.go, chi, uuid) is identical across every module — or there is exactly one module.
- [ ] A future divergence **fails the gate**: by construction if collapsed, by an explicit check if not.
- [ ] CI and `make check` stay mirrored.
- [ ] No dependency major is bumped in the same diff.
- [ ] `make check` and a full `docker compose up` both green, with regenerated code committed **before** the gate run.

**Sequencing note:** do not land concurrently with TKT-126 (which edits `shared/go`).

objective.note: Eight Go modules in one repo with one deploy unit have produced visible dependency version drift. Either collapse them or make drift fail the gate — silently diverging shared dependencies across services is the failure mode to close.

scope.note: IN: making the shared dependency set consistent across modules, by collapsing to one go.mod or by adding a drift check to make check; whichever path is taken, the go.work/Dockerfile/CI consequences are carried through and CI stays mirrored with the local gate. OUT: upgrading any dependency to a new major; changing service boundaries (the modules are a build-layout question, not an architecture one).

uncertainties.note: Collapse to one module vs keep eight and gate on drift. Collapse is simpler to live with (one dependency set, no check to maintain) but touches every Dockerfile, go.work and CI job; the drift check is a smaller diff that leaves the maintenance. The plan picks after measuring the Dockerfile/CI blast radius. Both satisfy the COS.

dependencies.note: None. Should not land concurrently with TKT-126 (shared/go changes) to avoid a needless conflict — sequencing note, not a blocker.

approach.note: Whatever path is chosen, the gate is the proof: CI and make check must stay mirrored (working agreement), and regenerated code is committed before the gate run — check-generate diffs against HEAD, so an uncommitted regen reads as drift and burns a gate run. Do not take the opportunity to bump majors; a version-alignment change that also upgrades is unreviewable.

first_slice.note: If the drift check is chosen it is the whole ticket. If collapse is chosen, the first slice is the module merge with go.work removed and every Dockerfile/CI path updated in the same PR — a half-collapsed build is worse than either end state, so this one does not split.

success.note: COS: (1) the shared dependency set (otel, kin-openapi, pgx, nats.go, chi, uuid) is identical across every module, or there is exactly one module; (2) a future divergence fails make check — by construction if collapsed, by an explicit check if not; (3) CI and make check remain mirrored; (4) no dependency major is bumped in the same diff; (5) make check and a full docker compose up both green, with regenerated code committed BEFORE the gate run.

context_memo.note: Baked: ADR-001 (the Go/TypeScript stack and the single-deploy-unit assumption that makes eight modules unnecessary), ADR-022 (each binary carries a migrate subcommand — a module collapse must not disturb the per-binary entrypoints or the one-shot Compose jobs). Working agreement: make check and CI stay mirrored; commit regenerated code before running the gate (cost two gate runs on TKT-114).

binding.rule: We build five Go services (catalog, inventory, commerce, payments, access) behind an API gateway, with an event bus for the domain event stream; every entity carries a tenant/organizer id from day one. Docker Compose only. The gateway is the only public surface, with explicit route registration.
Migrations run out-of-band: each binary's `migrate` subcommand, as a one-shot Compose job the service waits on. The server path never migrates.

# TKT-129 execution plan

## Decision

Choose **option 2: retain the eight modules and add a dependency-declaration drift gate**.

The supported build already uses one MVS-selected dependency set because every current Go command discovers the root `go.work`. The defect is therefore not that concurrently deployed services currently use different versions. It is that:

- changing one manifest can silently change the workspace-selected version for every binary;
- the other manifests remain stale, hiding that blast radius during review;
- `go mod tidy` updates one module, not its siblings;
- a later `go work sync` fans the change back across manifests;
- modules capable of running outside the workspace could select another graph—although the five services are not currently standalone-capable because they do not declare or replace `ticketing/shared`.

A fast declaration check closes that failure mode with substantially less churn than collapsing the modules.

## 1. Blast-radius measurement

### Verified tree facts

All eight module paths and `go.work` entries match the brief.

The four additional declaration mismatches also match:

- `github.com/gorilla/mux`: smoke `v1.8.0`, catalog/shared `v1.8.1`
- `golang.org/x/crypto`: smoke `v0.54.0`, five services `v0.52.0`
- `golang.org/x/sys`: smoke `v0.47.0`, five services/shared `v0.45.0`
- `golang.org/x/text`: smoke `v0.40.0`, five services/shared `v0.37.0`

One measured fact in the brief is wrong: `compose.yaml` contains **12** `PKG:` occurrences, not 7. They are five server builds, five migration jobs, the access lifecycle-backfill job, and gateway.

### Workspace resolution: what is actually drifting

`go env GOWORK` at the root and from a service resolves to the repository’s `go.work`. Targeted `go list -m` calls from the root, catalog, and smoke all selected the same relevant workspace versions, including:

- `otel v1.44.0`
- `kin-openapi v0.142.0`
- `mux v1.8.1`
- `x/crypto v0.54.0`
- `x/sys v0.47.0`
- `x/text v0.40.0`

With `GOWORK=off`, catalog instead reports `otel v1.43.0` transitively and `x/text v0.37.0`. More importantly, `GOWORK=off go list ./...` fails for all five services because imports such as `ticketing/shared/obs` have no standalone `require`/`replace`. Gateway and smoke do not have that internal-module problem.

Therefore:

- The per-module loops in `Makefile` are **not isolated builds**; `cd` does not disable the parent workspace.
- `go test ./...` from any service uses the union workspace graph.
- `go mod tidy` updates only the current module’s declarations and sums; it does not synchronize sibling manifests.
- `go work sync` is the Go-provided operation that raises each manifest’s declared versions to the workspace build list.
- `go.work.sum` is supplementary checksum data, not a lockfile or an authoritative selected-version list. It contains, for example, OTel `v1.43.0` metadata while the workspace selects `v1.44.0`.

The full `go list -m all` attempt could not finish in this read-only environment because uncached transitive module metadata required network/cache writes. Targeted `go list -m` and the installed Go 1.26.5 workspace help were sufficient to verify the relevant selection behavior.

### Option 1: one root `go.mod`

The coherent minimum is **61 changed paths**.

#### Module metadata: 19 paths

Create:

- `go.mod`
- `go.sum`

Delete:

- `go.work`
- `go.work.sum`
- `gateway/go.mod`
- `services/{access,catalog,commerce,inventory,payments}/go.mod`
- `shared/go/go.mod`
- `smoke/go.mod`
- `services/{access,catalog,commerce,inventory,payments}/go.sum`
- `shared/go/go.sum`
- `smoke/go.sum`

#### Shared imports: 28 Go files

A root module named `ticketing` maps `shared/go/domainevent` to `ticketing/shared/go/domainevent`. It therefore requires rewriting all 28 files that import `ticketing/shared/...`:

- `gateway/cmd/gateway/main.go`
- `services/access/cmd/access/main.go`
- `services/access/internal/api/server.go`
- `services/access/internal/consumer/{consumer,policy,run}.go`
- `services/access/internal/store/alarm_envelope.go`
- `services/catalog/cmd/catalog/main.go`
- `services/catalog/internal/api/server.go`
- `services/catalog/internal/events/events.go`
- `services/commerce/cmd/commerce/main.go`
- `services/commerce/internal/api/{server,server_test}.go`
- `services/commerce/internal/events/events.go`
- `services/inventory/cmd/inventory/main.go`
- `services/inventory/internal/api/{operational,reservations,server}.go`
- `services/inventory/internal/consumer/{consumer,run}.go`
- `services/payments/cmd/payments/main.go`
- `services/payments/internal/api/server.go`
- `services/payments/internal/psp/{fake,fake_test}.go`
- `shared/go/domainevent/envelope_test.go`
- `shared/go/httpx/healthz_test.go`
- `shared/go/obs/{obs,requestlog}_test.go`

Moving the 18 non-manifest files from `shared/go` to `shared/` would preserve the imports, but it is not cheaper: at least 17 outside files reference the physical `shared/go` path, including tests, gate scripts, architecture documentation, and accepted ADRs. That produces at least 35 touched logical files versus 28 import rewrites and changes the documented shared-kernel location.

A `replace ticketing/shared => ./shared/go` cannot avoid this while retaining exactly one module; a local replacement target must itself be a module.

#### Build, automation, and documentation: 14 paths

- `Makefile`
- `build/go.Dockerfile`
- `.github/dependabot.yml`
- `.github/workflows/{check,hermetic,security}.yaml`
- `docs/architecture.md`
- `docs/development.md`
- `docs/docker.md`
- `docs/testing.md`
- `docs/technical-delivery-standards.md`
- `docs/conventions/dependencies-and-versions.md`
- `docs/adr/ADR-034-shared-durable-consumer-lifecycle.md`
- new dependency-layout ADR

No Compose file needs changing if the root module is `ticketing`; all 12 existing service/gateway `PKG` import paths remain valid. The six binaries and five migration jobs remain separate.

The catalog `tool` directive would move to the root `go.mod`. Existing `cd services/catalog... && go tool oapi-codegen` commands can remain because Go discovers the parent root module and their relative output paths remain correct.

A root `go build ./...` would not build the 18 tagged smoke integration tests: they are `_test.go` files and carry `//go:build smoke`. It would build `smoke/internal/loadtest`, whose two Go files are untagged. Root `go test ./...` would newly run that package’s untagged unit test during `test-go`; the tagged smoke suite would remain owned by `scripts/smoke.sh`.

### Option 2: retain modules and gate drift

The planned implementation is **21 changed paths**:

- 14 existing dependency files
- 3 gate implementation/test files
- 4 documentation files

Dockerfiles, Compose, `go.work`, CI workflows, Dependabot configuration, package imports, generated code, and service entrypoints remain untouched.

## 2. Why option 2 wins

The collapse option is architecturally tidy but closes no current runtime split: workspace MVS already selects one graph, Docker builds from that workspace, and the services are not independently buildable outside it.

Against that, collapse changes 61 paths, including 28 imports, dependency automation, three CI workflows, and several current-topology documents. Keeping the modules requires 21 paths, most of which are mechanical `go.mod`/`go.sum` alignment.

Option 2 also preserves:

- ADR-002’s five service binaries;
- ADR-022’s per-binary `migrate` entrypoints and Compose jobs;
- ADR-009’s catalog-owned `tool` directive and generator working directories;
- the `shared/go` kernel location established by ADR-033/034;
- all existing Docker `PKG` arguments.

## 3. The test seam

Add a new phony Make target, `check-go-dependency-drift`, and make it an early prerequisite of `check`.

A new `scripts/check-go-dependency-drift.sh` will:

1. Receive the eight `go.mod` paths from `GO_MODULES`.
2. Run `GOWORK=off go mod edit -json <path>` for each. This parses manifests without loading packages, downloading modules, or consulting workspace MVS.
3. Extract every direct and indirect `require` tuple: dependency path, version, owning module.
4. Group by dependency path.
5. Ignore dependencies declared by only one module.
6. Fail if any dependency declared by two or more modules has more than one version, printing all conflicting module/version pairs.

This is intentionally broader than the six named dependencies, so the present `mux` and `x/*` drift is covered without maintaining an allowlist. An absent declaration is not treated as a version: forcing every module to pin unused dependencies would fight `go mod tidy` and would not describe actual package usage.

### Seeded negative proof

Extend `scripts/gate-selftest.sh` with:

1. A clean-baseline assertion that `make check-go-dependency-drift` succeeds.
2. A seed that changes access’s direct OTel requirement from `v1.44.0` to `v1.43.0` using `go mod edit`.
3. `expect_fail "Go dependency drift" check-go-dependency-drift`.

The baseline assertion prevents an always-failing or missing checker from satisfying the negative test. The disposable worktree and existing reset logic restore the manifest after the seed.

The production check runs in `make check`. The destructive meta-test remains in the separate existing `gate-selftest` CI job, like the other seeded lint/test/build failures; putting self-mutation inside `make check` would recursively sabotage the normal gate. CI already runs both jobs.

## 4. Definition of Done

1. **One version per shared dependency declaration.**  
   Evidence: `make check-go-dependency-drift` passes, and its extracted records show a singleton version for OTel, kin-openapi, pgx, nats.go, chi, and uuid.

2. **Future divergence fails.**  
   Evidence: the gate self-test starts clean, seeds access OTel `v1.43.0`, observes `make check-go-dependency-drift` exit non-zero, then completes successfully because the seeded defect was caught.

3. **CI and local gate remain mirrored.**  
   Evidence: `.github/workflows/check.yaml` remains unchanged at `run: make check`; the new target is a `check` prerequisite. The existing separate `gate-selftest` job proves the negative seam.

4. **No dependency major is bumped.**  
   Evidence: the only requirement changes are:
   - mux `v1.8.0 → v1.8.1`
   - x/crypto `v0.52.0 → v0.54.0`
   - x/sys `v0.45.0 → v0.47.0`
   - x/text `v0.37.0 → v0.40.0`

   The pre/post workspace `go list -m` snapshot is identical for these dependencies, proving supported builds were already selecting the destination versions.

5. **Repository and runtime gates pass.**  
   Evidence: generated artifacts are regenerated and committed before running `make check`; then `make check`, `scripts/gate-selftest.sh`, and `make up`/`docker compose up --build --wait` pass. `docker compose ps --all` shows all migration/init jobs exited zero and long-running services healthy.

## 5. Files to change

### Gate and proof

- `Makefile`
  - Add `check-go-dependency-drift` to `.PHONY`.
  - Add it as an early `check` prerequisite.
  - Pass all `$(GO_MODULES)/go.mod` paths to the checker.

- `scripts/check-go-dependency-drift.sh` — new
  - POSIX shell plus `go mod edit -json`, `awk`, and `sort`.
  - No `jq`, network access, or third-party tool.
  - Stable diagnostics naming dependency, module, and conflicting version.

- `scripts/gate-selftest.sh`
  - Add clean positive control.
  - Seed an OTel mismatch.
  - Require the new target to reject it.

### Declaration normalization

- `services/access/{go.mod,go.sum}`
- `services/catalog/{go.mod,go.sum}`
- `services/commerce/{go.mod,go.sum}`
- `services/inventory/{go.mod,go.sum}`
- `services/payments/{go.mod,go.sum}`
  - Raise x/crypto to `v0.54.0`, x/sys to `v0.47.0`, x/text to `v0.40.0`.

- `shared/go/{go.mod,go.sum}`
  - Raise x/sys to `v0.47.0`, x/text to `v0.40.0`.

- `smoke/{go.mod,go.sum}`
  - Raise gorilla/mux to `v1.8.1`.

Use the workspace-selected higher versions rather than downgrading smoke. Although downgrading smoke would touch fewer manifests, it would change the versions used by supported builds. Raising declarations makes the manifest diff larger but leaves the actual workspace build list unchanged.

`go.work.sum` is expected to remain unchanged.

### Documentation

- `docs/adr/ADR-035-go-module-dependency-governance.md` — new, assuming ADR-035 remains free
  - Record the measured 61-versus-21-path decision.
  - State the declaration-only guarantee and why it is not a claim of current runtime divergence.
  - Record collapse as the rejected alternative and its trigger for reconsideration.

- `docs/conventions/dependencies-and-versions.md`
  - Document that repeated Go requirements must use one version and are gate-enforced.

- `docs/testing.md`
  - Add the dependency check to the gate-stage table.
  - Add the seeded drift case to the gate-self-test description.

- `docs/technical-delivery-standards.md`
  - Add the dependency-declaration stage and update the self-test description.

If ADR-035 is taken by another merged ticket before implementation, allocate the next free number and update only its references.

## 6. Test-first execution order

1. Capture the pre-change workspace-selected dependency list with `go list -m`.
2. Add the Make target wiring and seeded gate-selftest case first. Because the self-test builds a worktree from `HEAD`, commit this red test seam before invoking it.
3. Use a temporary success-only checker stub or the missing implementation to observe the self-test red: the clean baseline or seeded mismatch is not correctly handled.
4. Implement the checker.
5. Run `make check-go-dependency-drift`; it must remain red, now for the four real mismatched dependency groups with useful diagnostics.
6. Normalize declarations to the existing workspace-selected versions, preferably starting with `go work sync`, then run `go mod tidy` in each changed module.
7. Inspect the diff. Abort and investigate if any manifest outside the named seven modules changes or any additional dependency moves.
8. Run the checker again; it must be green.
9. Commit the checker and normalized manifests, then run `scripts/gate-selftest.sh`. Its baseline must pass and its seeded OTel divergence must be caught.
10. Run `make generate`. Commit any regenerated output before the full gate; no generated change is expected because the catalog tool version remains `v2.7.2`.
11. On a clean commit, run `make check`.
12. Run the full hermetic stack with `make up`, which executes `docker compose up -d --build --wait`, and inspect all job/service states.

## 7. Risks and traps

- **Mistaking declaration drift for simultaneous runtime version drift.**  
  Mitigation: the ADR and checker name the guarantee precisely. Supported workspace builds already use one MVS list.

- **Comparing `go.sum` or `go.work.sum`.**  
  Those files contain checksums for historical/transitive metadata and may legitimately mention several versions. The checker reads only `require` declarations through Go’s parser.

- **Forcing every module to declare all six dependencies.**  
  Unused pins are removed by `go mod tidy` and misrepresent package ownership. Compare versions only where a dependency is declared.

- **Changing the supported build graph while normalizing.**  
  Align upward to the versions already selected by workspace MVS. Compare the pre/post `go list -m` snapshots; they must be identical.

- **Accidentally including a major upgrade.**  
  Review the exact four version transitions above and reject any extra `go.mod` line. The unchanged workspace build snapshot provides an independent control.

- **A checker that always fails passing its negative test.**  
  Gate self-test must assert the clean baseline succeeds before seeding divergence.

- **Shell portability.**  
  Use POSIX shell/awk/sort constructs and `LC_ALL=C`; do not depend on GNU-only flags or installed `jq`.

- **Gate latency.**  
  `go mod edit -json` is local metadata parsing and should complete in milliseconds. Do not use `go list -m all`, downloads, or per-module builds inside the new target.

- **Docker failure invisible to `make check`.**  
  The normal smoke stage packages host-built binaries with `build/go-bin.Dockerfile`; it does not exercise the hermetic `build/go.Dockerfile`. Full Compose can still fail on module downloads, image-layer invalidation, CGO/static compilation, the five `migrate` entrypoints, `service_completed_successfully` ordering, or healthchecks. This is why full `make up` remains mandatory.

- **CI cache behavior.**  
  No cache path changes. `actions/setup-go` continues hashing `**/go.sum`; changed sum content produces a normal cache miss, not a broken cache. The golangci cache key also naturally rotates. Because `go.mod`/`go.sum` paths change, both hermetic and security workflows are already triggered.

- **Gate self-test uses committed HEAD.**  
  Uncommitted checker/test changes are invisible to its disposable worktree. Commit before running that proof.

- **Unexpected generator drift.**  
  The catalog `tool` directive stays in `services/catalog/go.mod`. Any generated diff is unexpected and must be understood rather than casually folded into this ticket.

## 8. Deliberately not done

- No module collapse: its 61-path blast does not buy a runtime correctness improvement today.
- No service, binary, database, migration-job, or Compose-boundary change.
- No Dockerfile, Compose, workflow, Dependabot, import-path, or `go.work` edit under the selected option.
- No new third-party checker dependency.
- No comparison against checksum files or complete transitive graphs.
- No artificial pinning of unused dependencies.
- No dependency-major or “latest version” upgrade.
- No separate CI drift step: `make check` is already the CI command.
- No UI/browser submission: no web write path is touched.
- No generated-file edit is expected; generation is still run and committed-before-gate discipline is preserved.

<!-- sdlc:stage=plan-review kind=summary -->
### Plan critique — TKT-129 · adversarial pass by `main-agent`

`config.models.planReview: main-agent`; the draft was written by `gpt-5.6-sol`. Distinct models, so
the cross-model invariant holds. Primed adversarially: I tried to falsify the draft's measurements
rather than confirm them, and I ran the experiments the draft could only reason about.

**Verdict: accept the decision, amend four sections, reject one.** No part of the draft is rejected
wholesale.

---

## A. Existence check — every path and symbol the draft names

Per the skill's rule that a drafter which couldn't run the gate will hallucinate seams, I checked
each named path at `HEAD`.

| Named by the draft | Exists? |
|---|---|
| `scripts/gate-selftest.sh` (+ its `expect_fail` helper, disposable-worktree reset) | ✅ real, and its shape matches the draft's use |

- **The six COS-named dependencies are already identical wherever declared** (otel 2/8 modules,

## C. Two experiments the draft could only reason about — I ran them

**C1. `go mod tidy` across all eight modules is a complete no-op — and leaves every drift group intact.**

```
tidy shared/go · services/{catalog,inventory,commerce,payments,access} · gateway · smoke
→ git diff: (empty)
→ drift groups remaining: 4   (gorilla/mux, x/crypto, x/sys, x/text)
```

This is the single most important measured fact in this ticket, and neither the ticket nor the draft
states it: **the repository is simultaneously fully tidy and fully drifted.** Tidy is drift-preserving,
so "just run `go mod tidy`" — the reflex answer, and the one a reviewer will propose — provably does
not close the failure mode. It also means the drift will *never* self-heal through normal maintenance.

**C2. `go work sync` is the only Go-provided operation that aligns them — and `go mod tidy` afterwards
does not revert it.**

I expected sync-then-tidy to flip-flop (sync raises, tidy prunes) and flagged it as a likely blocking
trap. **My hypothesis was wrong.** Measured: `go work sync` → `go mod tidy` in each module → `go work
sync` again reaches a **fixpoint** with no further change. Recording this as *refuted* rather than
quietly dropping it: the draft's step-6 ordering is safe, and the only thing wrong with its trailing
`go mod tidy` is that it is a **no-op**, not a hazard.

Cost: `go work sync` is **0.19s warm** and idempotent; ~5min on a cold module cache.

## D. Findings — per-part verdicts

**D1 · Decision: option 2 (keep eight modules, gate the drift) — ACCEPT.**
The reasoning survives scrutiny. Collapse buys no runtime correctness today because the workspace
already selects one graph and the services are not standalone-buildable. 61 paths versus 21, and it
would disturb the `shared/go` kernel location that ADR-033/034 just established. It is also the more
reversible end state, which is the tie-break this gateless run is required to apply.

**D2 · DoD item 4's evidence list — REJECT as written.** The draft claims "the only requirement
changes are" four version transitions. I ran the normalization; that is **factually incomplete**. The
true change set of `go work sync`:

*Version raises (8, all pre-existing workspace selections, zero major changes — no `vN` path moves):*
`gorilla/mux 1.8.0→1.8.1` · `x/crypto 0.52.0→0.54.0` · `x/sync 0.21.0→0.22.0` · `x/sys 0.45.0→0.47.0`
· `x/text 0.37.0→0.40.0` · `x/mod 0.35.0→0.37.0` · `x/tools 0.44.0→0.47.0` · `x/net 0.55.0→0.56.0`

*Newly declared indirect requirements (5, all test-only, pulled from the workspace build list):*
`davecgh/go-spew` · `pmezard/go-difflib` · `kr/pretty` · `rogpeppe/go-internal` · `google/go-cmp`

*Plus a new empty `gateway/go.sum`* (the gateway has no dependencies).

Measured diff: **14 files, +98/−107**. COS 4 still holds — nothing changes major version — but the
DoD must be evidenced against the real list, not a subset of it.

**D3 · Step 7's abort condition — AMEND, it would abort this run.** As written ("abort if … any
additional dependency moves") the plan halts on its own normalization, because five requirements are
*added* and four more versions move beyond the named four. Replace with an explicit expected-diff
allowlist: the 8 raises + 5 additions + `gateway/go.sum` above, `go.work.sum` unchanged, no `.go`
file touched, no major-version path change. Anything outside that list aborts.

**D4 · Step 3's "temporary success-only checker stub" — AMEND, cut it.** Manufacturing a stub to
observe red is theatre when the tree contains **four real drift groups**. Write the real checker,
wire it into `make check`, and watch it fail on production data *before* normalizing — that is a
genuine TDD red on the actual defect. Step 5 already describes exactly this, so step 3 is redundant.
Order: checker red on real drift → normalize → green → commit → seed a synthetic divergence in
`gate-selftest.sh` to prove it stays red for *future* drift.

**D5 · The negative proof living in `gate-selftest.sh`, outside `make check` — ACCEPT.** Worth
stating because it looks like a gap and is not. COS 2 ("a future divergence fails the gate") is
satisfied by the checker *inside* `make check`; `gate-selftest.sh` proves the checker is not a
no-op, and it is the established home for every seeded-defect proof in this repo. Both run in CI.
The draft's insistence on a clean-baseline positive control before seeding is right — without it, an
always-failing checker passes its own negative test.

**D6 · Documentation set — ACCEPT all four, against my prior.** I went in expecting to cut this as
gold-plating and could not. `docs/testing.md` carries a per-stage gate table; `docs/technical-delivery-standards.md`
states in prose that the self-test "proves that seeded lint, test, and build defects fail the gate";
`docs/conventions/dependencies-and-versions.md` already says "Dependabot checks all eight Go modules".
A new gate stage absent from all three is documentation drift — the same class of defect this ticket
closes. ADR-035 records the rejected collapse. All four are one-paragraph edits.

## E. Introduced at plan-review — reviewed by no second model

Per the skill, everything I *added* rather than accepted, amended or rejected. These reach the
(waived) Gate 2 having been seen only by their author, me.

**E1 · Dependabot is the drift generator, and the plan does not mention it.** `.github/dependabot.yml`
runs `gomod` weekly over all eight module directories **with no `groups:` key** — so it opens
per-module PRs. Once this checker lands, any Dependabot PR bumping a dependency that a sibling module
also declares will **fail the gate**, and the fix is a follow-up `go work sync` commit on that PR.
That is the check working as designed, not a defect — but it is a foreseeable weekly operational cost
that nobody has consented to yet. **Decision: name it in ADR-035 and in
`docs/conventions/dependencies-and-versions.md`, make the checker's failure message say
`run: go work sync`, and do *not* add Dependabot grouping in this diff** (out of scope, and grouping
is a separate judgement call about update batching). If it proves annoying, that is a new ticket with
its own evidence.

**E2 · `gateway/go.sum` is created empty by `go work sync` and must be committed.** Otherwise every
subsequent run re-creates an untracked file. Immaterial to the chosen `go mod edit -json` checker
(it reads `go.mod` only) — but it *would* have been a silent hole in a `git diff --exit-code`-style
check, since `git diff` does not see untracked files.

**E3 · The checker must skip the `go` and `toolchain` directives.** They are not `require` tuples,
and `go mod edit -json` reports them in separate fields — trivially handled, but an unstated
assumption in the draft's step 3.

**E4 · `go work sync && git diff --exit-code` was considered as a two-line alternative to the
checker script and is REJECTED.** It mirrors the existing `check-generate` idiom exactly, needs no
new file, and runs in 0.19s warm — genuinely tempting, and the laziest thing that could work. Three
measured reasons it loses: it took **~5 minutes on a cold module cache** and may need network, which
is a direct threat to the ~2min gate TKT-42 paid for; it **mutates the working tree during the gate**;
and it cannot see the untracked `gateway/go.sum` (E2). `go mod edit -json` is pure offline parsing at
~0.2s. Recording the rejection with its reason so this does not get re-litigated in code review.

## F. Pre-mortem — this ticket shipped and something went wrong

- *"It merged and the gate never actually ran the check."* → The checker is a prerequisite of `check`,
  and `gate-selftest.sh` seeds a divergence and asserts failure. Both in CI.
- *"The checker passes because it compares nothing."* → The clean-baseline positive control in the
  self-test, plus the fact that it must be observed **red on the four real drift groups** before
  normalization (D4).
- *"We claimed we fixed version drift; we only fixed the manifests."* → ADR-035 must state the
  guarantee in the ADR-021 register: this closes **declaration** drift under an honest maintainer. It
  does not and cannot constrain someone editing a `go.mod` and the checker together, and there is no
  runtime divergence today to fix.
- *"`docker compose up` broke and `make check` was green."* → Real: the smoke stage packages
  host-built binaries via `build/go-bin.Dockerfile` and never exercises the hermetic
  `build/go.Dockerfile`. COS 5 requires the full `make up`, and it is not optional.
- *"A dependency major slipped in."* → Checked mechanically against the 8-raise list in D2: no module
  path changes `vN`. The `x/*` packages are pre-1.0 by upstream policy, so a minor bump is the
  largest step available.
